implementation_notes: lapin exposes an async AMQP 0-9-1 channel: the outbound half is channel.basic_publish(exchange, routing_key, options, payload, properties).await returning a publisher confirm, and the inbound half is the Consumer stream from basic_consume, iterated with StreamExt::next() and acknowledged via basic_ack. Ownership is static, so the adapter is a struct that owns a Channel (Clone + Send + Sync, internally synchronized) and is generic over the application handler trait - trait bounds replace the classic handler interface. Choose this variant for RabbitMQ/AMQP with tokio or async-std; keep the stream alive and re-subscribe after connection errors (wait_for_recovery).
pitfalls: Dropping the Consumer cancels consumption silently: the adapter must keep the stream alive and wait_for_recovery (or resubscribe) after a connection error.
Awaiting the publisher confirm on every message serialises throughput; ignoring it loses the delivery guarantee the caller assumes - choose deliberately.
Handlers that hold references across await points must be Send; blocking work inside the async adapter belongs in spawn_blocking.

variants.name: rdkafka FutureProducer + StreamConsumer
variants.implementation_notes: Kafka's Rust client models both directions as futures and streams: FutureProducer::send returns a future resolving to the partition/offset, and StreamConsumer::stream() yields BorrowedMessages without explicit polling, so the adapter becomes a thin async pipeline (`while let Some(m) = stream.next().await`) that maps payloads to application calls. Choose this variant when the transport is Kafka and the application is futures-based; unlike the AMQP variant the consumer needs a topic subscription and an explicit commit strategy rather than per-message acknowledgement.
pitfalls: The stream must be polled at least every max.poll.interval.ms or the group treats the process as dead (KIP-62 liveness) and rebalances.
The default auto-commit timer can advance past unprocessed messages; a slow handler needs explicit CommitMode::Async/manual commits.
BorrowedMessage borrows from the consumer: buffering messages beyond the loop body requires converting/owning the payload first.
